Cardiac magnetic resonance provides accurate quantification of ventricular volumes, the regurgitant volume and fraction, and myocardial remodeling and is particularly useful when echocardiographic findings are inconclusive or discordant. Computed tomography, owing to its high spatial resolution, offers detailed information on the mitral apparatus, annulus, calcifications, and anatomical relationships, supporting the planning of surgical and transcatheter procedures. The integration of echocardiography, CMR, and CT enables more comprehensive risk stratification and personalized treatment selection. The review highlights how multimodality imaging is now essential for guiding the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway, improving intervention timing, the procedural choice, and the overall management of patients with mitral regurgitation.

title: Longitudinal Trajectories of the Atherogenic Index of Plasma and Their Associations with Clinical Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
authors: Lihan Wang; Wenjing Sheng; Chengyi Zhang; Qifeng Zhu; Boren Tan; Feiyu Wu; Xianbao Liu
abstract: Background/Objectives: The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) reflects atherogenic dyslipidemia, but the clinical relevance of its longitudinal patterns after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear. We aimed to characterize AIP trajectories and explore their associations with clinical outcomes and echocardiographic changes after TAVR. Methods: This retrospective analysis included 1548 patients with at least two AIP measurements from within 7 days before TAVR through follow-up. Group-based trajectory modeling was used to identify longitudinal AIP patterns. Cox proportional hazards models and linear mixed-effects models were applied to assess clinical outcomes and longitudinal echocardiographic changes, respectively. Because trajectory assignment incorporated post-TAVR measurements, the analyses were considered exploratory. Results: Three distinct AIP trajectories were identified: low-level (n = 431, 27.8%), intermediate-level (n = 807, 52.1%), and high-level (n = 310, 20.0%). Higher trajectories were characterized by less favorable cardiometabolic profiles. Compared with the low-level trajectory, neither the intermediate-level trajectory (adjusted HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60-1.16; p = 0.277) nor the high-level trajectory (adjusted HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.74-1.61; p = 0.663) was significantly associated with major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. No significant associations with all-cause mortality or longitudinal echocardiographic recovery were detected. Conclusions: Distinct longitudinal AIP trajectories characterized different cardiometabolic profiles after TAVR, but no statistically significant association with major clinical outcomes or echocardiographic recovery was detected. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given temporal overlap in trajectory ascertainment, selection related to repeated measurements, and limited event numbers.

title: An inverse-protein-folding pre-trained model for predicting the mutational effects in protein-protein interactions.
authors: Sihong Mao; Siwei Meng; Ye Xiang
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in PPIs is crucial for protein engineering and drug discovery. Most existing PPI prediction approaches rely on refined physicochemical features or computationally intensive structural sampling. Here, we present delta-G message-passing-neural-network (DGMPNN), a message-passing neural-network framework for predicting the effects of mutations on PPIs. DGMPNN is pre-trained on an inverse protein folding (IPF) task and employs an adaptive residue-level attention pooling mechanism to enable effective transfer learning for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein binding affinity. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets and deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets. Experimental validation using computationally selected multi-site variants of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-hACE2 complex showed strong agreement between predicted and experimentally measured binding affinities.

title: Learning Adaptive Filtering in the Fourier Domain for Fringe Pattern Analysis: A New Reconstruction Paradigm in Digital Holographic Interferometry.
authors: Youxing Li; Lingzhi Meng; Zhiyuan Xu; Hongwei Li; Kai Zhang; Yaoqing Xie; Libo Yuan
abstract: Single-frame fringe pattern analysis in digital holographic interferometry (DHI) is essential for precision phase measurement under dynamic conditions. Recent advances in deep learning within optical metrology are transforming the reconstruction paradigm from physics-based modeling toward data-driven learning. However, most existing neural networks either rely on learning statistical visual features without guidance from physical principles or fail to dynamically adjust inference parameters based on the input instance after training, thereby limiting the robustness and generalization capacity on unseen data. To this end, a novel adaptive spectrum filtering neural network (ASFNet) is proposed for phase measurement. ASFNet incorporates a physics-aware spectral filtering block that dynamically adapts the inference process to each input instance, enabling robust and generalizable phase reconstruction under varying and unseen conditions-moving beyond static, dataset-specific statistical modeling toward instance-aware adaptive reconstruction. Moreover, a forward model is constructed to generate realistic simulation data for network training, reducing the reliance on experimentally labeled data. Simulation results on 400 test samples demonstrate the superiority of ASFNet in terms of both pixel-wise accuracy and visual quality. Experimental results further confirm its strong generalization capability on unseen data, achieving high reconstruction fidelity comparable to that of hand-tuned, physics-based methods.

title: Online forecasting for financial time series.
authors: Nikolas Michael; Mihai Cucuringu; Sam Howison
journal: International journal of data science and analytics
abstract: We introduce OFTER (online forecasting via temporal embedding regression), a time series forecasting pipeline tailored for financial problems centered on mid-sized multivariate time series. OFTER utilizes the non-parametric models of k-nearest neighbors and generalized regression neural networks, integrated with a dimensionality reduction component. To circumvent the curse of dimensionality, we employ a weighted norm based on a modified version of the maximal correlation coefficient. The pipeline we introduce is specifically designed for online tasks, has an interpretable output, and is able to outperform several state-of-the-art baselines. The computational efficacy of the algorithm, its online nature, and its ability to operate in low signal-to-noise regimes, render OFTER an ideal approach for financial multivariate time series problems, such as daily equity forecasting. Our work demonstrates that while deep learning models hold significant promise for time series forecasting, traditional methods carefully integrating mainstream tools remain very competitive alternatives with the added benefits of scalability and interpretability.

title: Designing an AI-Responsive Early Childhood Curriculum: A Conceptual Framework for Supporting Developmental Learning Trajectories in Preschool Education.
authors: Herlina Herlina; Chandra Apriyansyah; Rusmayadi Rusmayadi; Herman Herman
abstract:
The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning technologies into education creates new opportunities for personalized learning in early childhood education (ECE). Yet limited research has examined how educators interpret and enact AI-responsive curriculum decisions in preschool settings, particularly in culturally diverse contexts.
This study explores educators' experiences in designing and implementing AI-responsive curricula and develops a conceptual framework explaining how AI can inform curriculum decision-making for young children without displacing teacher judgment.
An interpretive phenomenological study was conducted at TK Harapan Bangsa, Makassar, Indonesia, with nine adult participants: six preschool teachers, two curriculum specialists, and one AI tool developer-collaborator whose expert interview supplied technical context. Data comprised two in-depth interviews with each teacher, interviews with curriculum specialists and the developer-collaborator, 18 non-participant observations, and analysis of AI-supported planning documents. MAXQDA 2024 supported data management. Giorgi's phenomenological method was operationalized through first-order meaning units, second-order interpretive themes, and third-order composite constructs. Triangulation, reflexive memoing, an audit trail, member checking, and peer debriefing supported trustworthiness.
Three interconnected constructs emerged. Predictive Developmental Tracking describes AI-supported identification of developmental readiness and possible concerns. AI-Responsive Curriculum Adaptation captures teachers' active interrogation and contextual modification of algorithmic recommendations. Deep Learning as Pedagogical Scaffold positions AI as a support that amplifies, rather than replaces, professional expertise. Together, the constructs informed the AI-Responsive Curriculum Design (ARCD) Framework.
The ARCD Framework explains AI-responsive curriculum implementation as a relational process combining predictive insight, ecological sensitivity, and educator agency. It offers implications for curriculum policy, teacher professional development, and ethical AI integration in ECE.

title: [Clinical reasoning in the age of artificial intelligence: the urgent need for formal education].
authors: Moshe Y Flugelman; Arieh Riskin
abstract:
Clinical reasoning remains the cornerstone of medical practice, yet unlike anatomy or physiology, medical curricula rarely teach it explicitly. This omission has significant consequences, as diagnostic errors account for up to 15% of adverse events in healthcare.
Theoretical models such as Dual Process Theory (System 1 intuitive vs. System 2 analytical reasoning), illness scripts, and metacognition highlight both the strengths and vulnerabilities of clinical cognition. The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical practice intensifies the need for structured reasoning education. While large language models demonstrate impressive diagnostic capabilities, risks such as automation bias and AI confabulations threaten safe decision-making.
Consequently, this review calls for a paradigm shift: clinical reasoning must become a formal, longitudinal core subject across all stages of medical education. In the AI era, clinical reasoning is not diminished; it is indispensable.

title: Diagnostic performance of multimodal large language models in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs.
authors: Bianca Marques de Mattos de Araujo; Maria Eduarda Cavassin; Allan Abuabara; Maria Luisa Giacon; Luiz Fernando Fariniuk; Christian Kirschneck; Michelle Nascimento Meger; Rafaela Scariot; Flares Baratto-Filho; Erika Calvano Küchler
abstract:
Pulp stones are calcified structures within the dental pulp that may increase the complexity of endodontic treatment and are commonly identified through radiographic examinations. Despite recent advances in artificial intelligence applied to dental imaging, the diagnostic capability of publicly available multimodal large language models (LLMs) for detecting pulp stones under zero-shot conditions remains unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the diagnostic performance and response consistency of multimodal LLMs in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs of posterior teeth.
This comparative and exploratory study evaluated the GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash multimodal LLMs using panoramic radiograph image crops containing posterior teeth. A total of 64 image crops, comprising 192 posterior teeth, were analyzed. The models were tested under standardized zero-shot conditions using independent sessions and a standardized English-language prompt. Each image was submitted six times to both models to assess response consistency. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1-score with 95% confidence intervals. Intra-model consistency was assessed using majority agreement, complete agreement across repetitions, and Fleiss' Kappa coefficient.
The models demonstrated similar overall accuracy for binary detection of pulp stones, with 56.5% for ChatGPT and 57.0% for Gemini. ChatGPT showed high specificity (96.2%) and greater intra-model stability, whereas Gemini demonstrated higher sensitivity (81.8%) and superior performance in identifying the affected tooth and dental group. However, Gemini also presented lower specificity and greater variability across repeated evaluations. Fleiss' Kappa coefficients indicated low intra-model agreement beyond chance for both models, particularly for Gemini.
Multimodal LLMs demonstrated limited capability in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs, with distinct diagnostic profiles between the evaluated models. Although the findings suggest potential future applications of LLMs as auxiliary tools for dental image interpretation, their current performance does not yet support consistent clinical applicability for pulp stone detection.

title: Multicenter external validation of a multimodal MRI deep-learning model to predict meningioma bone invasion.
authors: Zhouyuan Wei; Wei Hu; Fuqiang Tang; Jialiang Ren; Junlin Zhou; Mengjia Liu; Ling Su; Jing Zhang
abstract:
Preoperative detection of meningioma bone invasion lacks objective biomarkers and relies on subjective radiological assessment, posing a risk of excessive bone resection or residual tumor. We therefore developed and externally validated a parsimonious six-feature DenseNet121 signature derived from multiparametric MRI across two independent institutions.
In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 438 consecutive patients (mean age, 53 ± 11 years; 77% women) with histologically confirmed meningioma were allocated to training (n = 182), internal validation (n = 77), and external test (n = 179) sets. Following N4 bias-field correction and isotropic resampling, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted volumes were fed into a DenseNet121 architecture to extract a six-feature signature via nested cross-validation. Discrimination (area under the ROC curve, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision-curve analysis) were evaluated.
In the external cohort (prevalence 11%), the signature achieved an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), sensitivity 75%, specificity 77% and negative predictive value 96%, with an AUC improvement of 0.155 over conventional radiomics (95% CI, 0.01-0.30; p = 0.035). At a 20% risk threshold, decision-curve analysis confirmed a positive net clinical benefit, primarily driven by the high negative predictive value. SHAP analysis demonstrated the dominant and consistent contribution of low-ADC features.
The DenseNet121-derived six-feature signature serves as a reliable rule-out aid for preoperative meningioma bone invasion, with a high negative predictive value that may safely support decisions to avoid extensive bone resection in predicted-negative cases. Positive predictions require confirmatory CT or intraoperative biopsy to mitigate false positives. This tool could assist nurses and surgeons in preoperative planning, facilitating personalized patient care and potentially reducing operative time and complications.

title: A hierarchical residual Swin transformer with dual-level locality compensation for accelerated MRI reconstruction.
authors: Jinhong Huang; Guanglong Sun; Xinzhen Li; Zihan Yang; Genjiao Zhou
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides high spatial resolution, excellent soft-tissue contrast, and reliable anatomical discrimination, and is therefore widely used in clinical diagnosis. However, long acquisition time still limits imaging efficiency and clinical throughput. Although convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deep learning approaches have shown considerable promise for reconstructing images from undersampled k-space data, existing methods frequently fail to preserve fine structural details and texture continuity under aggressive undersampling conditions. In this study, we propose a novel reconstruction network based on the Swin Transformer, which integrates three key components: (i) long residual connections to facilitate the recovery of high-frequency details; (ii) a dual-level locality compensation mechanism to restore local spatial information; and (iii) a channel recalibration module to explicitly capture global dependencies among channels, thereby enhancing global feature extraction. Extensive experiments conducted on the IXI and MICCAI 2013 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms several compared generative adversarial network (GAN)-based approaches for MRI reconstruction across all undersampling mask types, achieving a PSNR improvement of approximately 0.6-1 dB over the best competing method under various settings. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cvgjhuor/HR-SwinGAN.

title: ThaCoder: an explainable deep learning framework for thalassemia screening using routine complete blood count: a multi-center validation study.
authors: Xiaosong Su; Yan Lin; Kouqiong Wang; Yuning Lin; Lin Wu; Xiang Jiang; Yi Shi; Baishen Pan; Beili Wang; Wei Guo; Jiaye Zhou
journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
abstract:
Thalassemia remains a global public health challenge, yet definitive diagnosis via genetic testing is often restricted by high costs and infrastructure requirements. We aimed to develop and externally evaluate an interpretable deep-learning framework using routine complete blood count (CBC) parameters for thalassemia screening.
Using 2317 CBC records from the internal derivation cohort, we implemented a two-stage analytical architecture. First, exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with Varimax rotation reduced nine continuous parameters to three factors, providing a lower-dimensional representation that attenuated multicollinearity among the erythrocyte indices. These latent factors, alongside gender, formed a 4-dimensional feature space that was processed through a deep neural network (DNN) optimized via a two-stage Bayesian-Grid search strategy and out-of-fold threshold selection. The locked model and operating threshold were evaluated without refitting or threshold reselection across four independent external centers (N = 1442).
In the internal test set, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.9598 and a specificity of 0.9337. External AUROC ranged from 0.8771 to 0.9439 across the four centers. Sensitivity was 0.8387 overall but was lower for silent α-thalassemia carriers (0.5270, 39/74) than for non-silent α-thalassemia carriers (0.8692, 226/260). SHAP-based interpretability indicated that the model's learned associations are consistent with the microcytic, hypochromic phenotype of thalassemia, with reduced MCV and MCH alongside a raised red-cell count emerging as the dominant drivers of a positive prediction. Health economic simulations suggest this algorithmic triage could reduce genetic-testing referrals and associated costs by approximately 76% in a preliminary 10%-prevalence illustration, although a subset of milder carriers is missed at the chosen threshold and the estimate is not a formal economic evaluation.
By integrating statistical feature engineering with deep learning, this framework provides a CBC-based pre-genetic-testing risk-stratification (triage) approach. The locked model and operating threshold were evaluated without refitting in four external centers, with between-center heterogeneity quantified, although absolute risk estimates require site-specific recalibration.

title: EsoEinstein: A Multimodal AI System Integrating EGD and FLIP for Esophageal Motility Assessment.
authors: Evandros Kaklamanos; Kristjana Kristinsdottir; Priyanka Soni; David Melnick; Wenjun Kou; Rajesh N Keswani; Dustin Carlson; Mozziyar Etemadi; John E Pandolfino
journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
abstract:
Achalasia diagnosis relies on integrating endoscopic, functional, and physiologic testing, yet high-resolution manometry (HRM) is invasive, uncomfortable, and resource limited. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a potential pathway to streamline this workflow. This study aimed to develop and validate AI models for diagnosing achalasia using esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), Functional Lumen Imaging Probe (FLIP) panometry, and their combined multimodal integration, using Chicago Classification v4.0 (CCv4.0) as the reference standard.
In this retrospective study, 1,802 adult patients who underwent HRM and had available EGD and/or FLIP data at a tertiary center were included. Separate deep learning models were trained for EGD videos, FLIP heatmap images, and a multimodal transformer that integrated both modalities. Primary outcomes were sensitivity, specificity, and AUC for detecting achalasia.
The 1,802-patient cohort was partitioned into training (n=1,522), validation (n=212), and test sets (n=68) for model development and evaluation. For the test set, the EGD model achieved sensitivity 0.724, specificity 0.974, and AUC 0.908. FLIP achieved sensitivity 0.862, specificity 0.821, and AUC 0.931. The multimodal model performed the best, with sensitivity 0.931, specificity 0.846, and AUC 0.969. Cochran's Q test found no statistically significant differences across models.
Multimodal AI that integrates endoscopic and FLIP data achieves expert-level accuracy and has potential as a less invasive approach for diagnosing achalasia. To realize this potential, future work must validate the system in real-world settings to evaluate its impact on diagnostic timelines and longitudinal patient outcomes.

title: Predicting Postoperative Outcomes in Small Rotator Cuff Tears: An AI-Based Approach to Long Head of the Biceps Management.
authors: Rayane Benhenneda; Thierry Brouard; Ramy Samargandi; Christophe Charousset; Julien Berhouet
abstract:
The management of the long head of the biceps (LHB) tendon in small rotator cuff tears remains controversial, particularly when the tendon appears macroscopically healthy. While prophylactic tenotomy or tenodesis is often recommended for pathological LHB, the decision-making process for an apparently normal LHB remains unclear. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an AI-based model for predicting postoperative outcomes in patients with small rotator cuff tears and a seemingly healthy LHB, assisting in the decision between preservation and tenotomy.
This was a prospective, multicenter, single-blind study including 199 patients with small rotator cuff tears. Preoperative clinical, imaging, and arthroscopic data were collected. A deep learning model, integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN) for arthroscopic image analysis and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for clinical and imaging data, was developed to predict the Constant score at 24 months follow-up. The model's predictions were compared with traditional statistical analyses, and subgroup analyses were performed on patients with a preserved healthy LHB and those with a poor functional outcome, defined by a Constant score <70 at follow-up.
The AI model accurately predicted the Constant score at 24 months in 91.4% of cases, with a mean prediction error of 6.04 points. In the "preserved healthy LHB" subgroup, the model achieved 93% accuracy, with a mean deviation of 5.45 points. However, in the "failed healthy LHB preserved" subgroup, accuracy dropped to 59.2%, with a mean deviation of 18 points. The AI model overestimated outcomes in 8 cases (leading to incorrect preservation of the LHB) and underestimated in 6 cases.
An AI model combining arthroscopic imaging and clinical data can predict postoperative Constant scores with high accuracy. However, its performance is limited in predicting failures, particularly in patients with a preserved LHB who later develop poor outcomes. While AI may complement conventional statistical methods in clinical decision-making, further validation with larger datasets and refined variables is necessary to enhance its reliability and clinical relevance.
III; Diagnostic Study.

title: Optimized Deep Knowledge Distillation Framework for Large-Scale Virus-Host Protein Interaction Prediction.
authors: Farzad Zandi; Parvaneh Mansouri
abstract:
In a rapidly evolving viral landscape, understanding virus-host protein interactions (VHPIs) is essential to elucidate viral infection mechanisms and support the development of effective therapeutic strategies. Accurate computational Prediction of VHPIs remains challenging because of the complexity and high dimensionality of protein sequence and functional representations.
We propose a Knowledge Distillation framework for pairwise VHPI prediction that integrates three teacher networks with a hybrid student architecture. Protein characteristics were represented using Conjoint Triad (CT), Dipeptide Composition (DC), Dipeptide Deviation from Expected Mean (DDE), Pseudo-Amino Acid Composition (PseAAC), amino acid encoding, and Gene Ontology (GO) features. We used tuned Monte Carlo ISUD for feature selection and compared it with five alternative approaches: PCA, MCFS, NMF, FA, and Optuna. We used an autoencoder to compress the one-hot encoded GO features. We evaluated on 25 randomly balanced datasets and one additional balanced dataset generated using NearMiss. Five-fold cross-validation was performed at the interaction-pair level using an 80:20 training-to-test ratio in each fold. The final configuration consisted of CT features, NearMiss-based data balancing, tuned MC-ISUD feature selection, and the Knowledge Distillation teacher-student framework.
The proposed framework achieved 92.91% accuracy and 96.16% AUC-ROC on the evaluated virus-host protein interaction datasets. Comparative experiments demonstrated that the proposed approach outperformed the existing methods considered in this study. These results are specific to the evaluated datasets and pairwise cross-validation design and should not be interpreted as evidence of generalization to completely unseen viral or host proteins.
The findings indicate that combining CT-based representation, NearMiss-based data balancing, tuned ISUD feature selection, and Knowledge Distillation provides a computational framework for pairwise VHPI prediction. The predictions should be regarded as computational hypotheses requiring independent experimental validation.

title: Relationship extraction for adverse drug events in clinical notes using large language models: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
authors: Joseph M Plasek; Yiming Li; Mary G Amato; Dinah Foer; Diane L Seger; Shayma Alzaidi; Huiyuan Zhou; Gretchen Purcell Jackson; David W Bates; Li Zhou
abstract:
Adverse drug events (ADEs) are a critical indicator of patient safety but are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. The potential of recent advances in natural language processing (NLP), particularly generative large language models (LLMs), to identify ADEs remains understudied. This study aimed to compare the performance of multiple LLMs in identifying ADE-Drug relationships in inpatient and ambulatory clinical notes.
We used clinical notes from the 2018 National NLP Clinical Challenge (n2c2) ADE dataset (inpatient; n = 505) and from outpatient encounters (n = 2555) between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, at a large academic medical center based in New England. Notes were pre-processed into snippets for model input. Evaluated Models included: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.2-3B and their instruction fine-tuned variants (including low-rank adapters for Llama). Performance was assessed using both strict and relaxed evaluations (precision, recall, and F1) for all models, followed by manual evaluation (exact semantic match, partial match, missing ADE, drug mention only, not a drug, or wrong) of the two best-performing models.
Of the 1048 notes in the local test split, 450 (42.9%) contained at least one ADE. The n2c2 test set included 202 notes, of which 155 (76.7%) contained at least one ADE. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini were the top-performing models among those evaluated. GPT-4o consistently outperformed GPT-4o-mini in ADE extraction across both datasets, with higher F1-scores (0.524 vs. 0.381) and a more balanced precision-recall profile. Both models captured ADEs effectively in explicit and complex clinical contexts, although limitations included misclassification of pre-existing allergies and occasional conflation of therapeutic indications with adverse effects. GPT-4o achieved higher exact match coverage and fewer errors across clinical notes, indicating more reliable performance in both inpatient and ambulatory settings.
This work establishes a foundation for integrating LLM methods into real-world drug safety surveillance, with direct implications for improving patient safety.

title: vToxiNet: An interpretable deep learning framework for hepatotoxicity prediction and mechanism exploration.
authors: Xuelian Jia; Tong Wang; Daniel P Russo; Lauren M Aleksunes; Shuo Xiao; Hao Zhu
abstract: Hepatotoxicity remains a leading cause of drug attrition and post-marketing withdrawal, resulting from diverse and complex toxicity mechanisms. Traditional in vitro models can only capture a limited subset of toxicity pathways, and animal studies face translational and ethical limitations. Regulatory agencies have therefore promoted new approach methodologies, including human-relevant assays, omics technologies, and computational models to improve predictive toxicology and support evidence-based decision-making. However, most machine learning models for hepatotoxicity either rely solely on chemical structure or operate as black boxes, limiting mechanistic interpretability and broader applicability. Here, we introduce the virtual toxicity network (vToxiNet), a biologically constrained deep learning framework that embeds systems toxicology knowledge directly into neural network architecture for interpretable hepatotoxicity prediction. vToxiNet integrates chemical descriptors, high-throughput assay responses, transcriptomic signatures, and Reactome pathway hierarchy to construct a virtual adverse outcome pathway network. Across cross-validation and external validation, vToxiNet demonstrates promising predictive performance. Importantly, interpretation of vToxiNet enables gene and pathway-level attribution, supporting mechanism-informed hazard characterization and chemical prioritization. By integrating multimodal data and biological hierarchy as architectural constraints, this study provides a framework that combines prediction with mechanistic interpretation and supports further development of mechanism-informed approaches for chemical hazard assessment.

title: UC-DiffuMambaNet: dual-scale state propagation and window attention for ordinal Mayo endoscopic grading.
authors: Pan Ma; Hao Zhou; Hao Wu; Yi Li; Guowu Yuan
abstract: Automated four-grade Mayo Endoscopic Score (MES) classification is challenging because inflammatory severity depends not only on subtle local mucosal changes, but also on the collective spatial pattern of abnormalities that may be separated across the visible field. We present UC-DiffuMambaNet, a hybrid architecture that integrates dual-scale severity-evidence propagation, two-dimensional contextual coordination, and hierarchical ordinal prediction. The Severity Mamba Mixer first strengthens informative mucosal features through locally gated multi-scale enhancement and then processes them with parallel short- and long-retention selective state-space branches. This design preserves local feature continuity while linking separated severity cues over complementary contextual ranges. Medical Window Attention subsequently coordinates fine intra-window structure with communication across windows, complementing state propagation with explicit two-dimensional spatial context. Finally, an Auxiliary Hierarchical Classification Head refines ordered MES assessment through feedback-guided hierarchical prediction. Across three independent seeds, UC-DiffuMambaNet achieved ACC/QWK/Macro-F1 of 91.26%/96.28%/90.70% on Dataset A and 79.95%/87.65%/74.17% on Dataset B (LIMUC). Compared with the architecture-matched MambaVision-T baseline, ACC increased by 3.01 and 2.90 percentage points, respectively. Factorial and internal ablations confirmed complementary contributions from the three modules. Together, these components provide an integrated framework for ordinal MES assessment.

title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
authors: Bin Hu; Zhongping Ai; Hui Xu; Liang Jiang; Hulin Kuang
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration.
authors: Majid Ramedani; Jaya C Terli; Ole H Martensen; Tobias Strauß; Katharina Buerger; Peter Dechent; Emrah Düzel; Klaus Fliessbach; Maria Gemenetzi; Wenzel Glanz; Julian Hellmann-Regen; Stefan Hetzer; Enise I Incesoy; Daniel Janowitz; Marie T Kronmüller; Christoph Laske; Falk Lüsebrink; Robert Perneczky; Oliver Peters; Lukas Preis; Josef Priller; Boris-Stephan Rauchmann; Ayda Rostamzadeh; Anja Schneider; Björn H Schott; Sebastian Sodenkamp; Annika Spottke; Eike J Spruth; Sophia Stöcklein; Jens Wiltfang; Frank Jessen; Stefan J Teipel; Martin Dyrba
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
abstract:
The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations.
Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration-specific metrics.
PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24).
This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.

title: Pediatric chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs using deep learning: a multicenter retrospective study.
authors: Jisun Hwang; Yisak Kim; Jae-Yeon Hwang; Kyungmin Jeon; Young Hun Choi
abstract:
Pelvic bones exhibit multiple secondary ossification centers during maturation, enabling automated age estimation. This study investigated whether a deep learning model could estimate chronological age from pelvic radiographs across the full pediatric age range.
This retrospective study included pelvic radiographs from two hospitals for model development, from patients aged between 0 and 18 years. A DenseNet161 model was trained to classify age into 19 1-year interval categories using chronological age as a reference standard and conditional ordinal regression (CORN) loss. External validation was conducted using two independent cohorts, including 541 radiographs from a different department of the same hospital and 203 from an external hospital. External validation was performed on 744 radiographs from two independent cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using the accuracy of predictions within 1 year of the chronological age (ACC@dist = 1) and the mean absolute error (MAE).
A total of 3972 radiographs (median age, 2.5 years; interquartile range, 0-8 years; 2463 males) were included in model development. On the internal test set, the model achieved an MAE of 0.394 years (girls: 0.360; boys: 0.419) and an ACC@dist = 1 of 0.937 (girls: 0.944; boys: 0.931). On the external test sets, the corresponding values were 0.513 years (girls, 0.628; boys, 0.455) and 0.927 (girls, 0.896; boys, 0.943), respectively.
Automated age estimation in children is feasible from pelvic radiography using a deep neural network.
Question Pelvic radiographs are commonly obtained in children, yet their potential for automated chronological age estimation across the full pediatric age range remains unexplored. Findings A deep learning model estimated chronological age from pelvic radiographs with a mean absolute error of 0.394 and 0.513 years on internal and external test sets, respectively. Clinical relevance Deep learning-based chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs is feasible across the full pediatric age range. This approach allows clinically relevant skeletal maturation data to be extracted from imaging already acquired for other indications.

title: Influence of virtual dynamic contrast enhanced breast MRI on lesion size, BI-RADS scores and reader confidence.
authors: Andrzej Liebert; Hannes Schreiter; Lorenz A Kapsner; Jessica Eberle; Chris M Ehring; Dominique Hadler; Sabine Ohlmeyer; Frederik B Laun; Ramona Erber; Julius Emons; Michael Uder; Evelyn Wenkel; Sebastian Bickelhaupt
abstract:
Breast MRI routinely uses gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) for dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging. However, GBCA administration entails periprocedural effort and environmental impact, prompting exploration of contrast-agent-free approaches. Deep learning-based virtual DCE (vDCE) offers a potential solution. This study evaluated vDCE against multiparametric DCE protocols, focusing on BI-RADS, background parenchymal enhancement (BPE), and lesion size.
This IRB-approved retrospective study included 592 3 T examinations divided into training, validation, and test sets. A 2D U-Net generated vDCE series from unenhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted acquisitions. Two board-certified radiologists evaluated vDCE and DCE examinations using a BI-RADS-adapted reading protocol. Diagnostic and ordinal outcomes were compared using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction.
Mean BI-RADS-based diagnostic accuracy was 76% for vDCE and 77% for DCE. Mean sensitivity was 92% vs 96%, and mean specificity was 65% vs 64%, respectively, without significant differences (both readers, p = 1.0). The mean paired lesion-size difference (DCE minus vDCE) was -2.2 mm in the holdout test set and 0.5 mm in the secondary test set. BPE (R1 p = 1.0; R2 p = 1.0) and artefact ratings (R1 p = 1.0; R2 p = 1.0) did not differ significantly. Reader confidence was high for both protocols, although lower for vDCE for one reader (p = 0.072).
vDCE showed four-percentage-point lower mean sensitivity and small, cohort-dependent lesion-size biases relative to GBCA-enhanced imaging. Further research is warranted to determine its potential role as a contrast-agent-free approach for selected breast imaging indications.
Question Breast MRI relies on GBCAs, creating procedural and environmental burdens, while clinically validated contrast-agent-free approaches for BI-RADS-based assessment remain unavailable. Findings Virtual DCE MRI showed lower sensitivity than standard DCE, no significant difference in BPE, but more variable reader confidence and lesion size presentation. Clinical relevance Virtual DCE breast MRI currently demonstrates limited diagnostic performance and requires further optimisation, while additional clinical validation studies are needed to determine its potential as a non-contrast alternative.

title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
authors: Sonali Patil; Meghana Lokhande; Shweta Koparde; Sonali Kothari; Sudan Jha
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

authors: Paolo Raggi; Marcelo Di Carli; Michelle Williams; Raffaele Giubbini; Diana Paez; Maurizio Dondi; Erick Alexanderson; Isabel Carvajal; Ayaz Aghayev; Alison Clifford; Dan Pugh; Neeraj Dhaun

title: https://impactfactor.org/PDF/IJDDT/16/IJDDT,Vol16,Issue88s,Article36.pdf
authors: Saurav Gupta; Shaurya Bhatnagar; Sharanya Ray; Priyadarshini S. Nayak; S S Rajput
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) carries a substantial burden of morbidity in developing countries, and its progression is driven by fibrosis of the valve apparatus and the left atrium. No current medical therapy targets this fibrotic process. Dapagliflozin, a sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor established across the heart failure spectrum, has demonstrated anti-fibrotic actions in experimental settings and favorable effects on left atrial (LA) function in clinical studies. Objective: To evaluate whether dapagliflozin alters circulating fibrosis biomarkers (TGF-β1, PICP, MMP1, TIMP-1), LA function and NT-proBNP in rheumatic MS, and whether biomarker changes correlate with functional changes. Methods: In an open-label, randomized controlled trial (July–December 2025), 33 adults with rheumatic MS (mitral valve area ≤ 1.5 cm², NYHA class II–III) received either dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily plus standard treatment (n = 17) or standard treatment alone (n = 16) for four weeks. TGF-β1, PICP, MMP-1, TIMP-1 and NT-proBNP were quantified by ELISA, and LA function was derived echocardiographically as net atrioventricular compliance (Cn) and mitral mean pressure gradient (MPG), at baseline and follow-up. Between-group comparisons of pre–post changes were analyzed; p < 0.05 was considered significant. Results: Groups were well matched at baseline. After four weeks, PICP and TGF-β1 had risen from baseline in both arms, while the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio fell (significant within the dapagliflozin arm, p = 0.005); between-group differences in the magnitude of these changes were not significant for any biomarker. NTproBNP decreased more in the dapagliflozin group than in the control group, with a significant betweengroup difference in change (p = 0.034), although follow-up values did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.449). Dapagliflozin significantly improved LA function - higher Cn and lower MPG - relative to control. Changes in fibrosis biomarkers correlated neither with changes in Cn nor with changes in NTproBNP. Conclusion: Four weeks of dapagliflozin improved LA function and NT-proBNP in rheumatic MS without a detectable between-group effect on circulating fibrosis biomarkers. Larger and longer trials using tissuelevel imaging are needed to establish whether dapagliflozin modifies disease progression. Keywords: dapagliflozin; SGLT2 inhibitor; rheumatic heart disease; mitral stenosis; atrial fibrosis; TGF-β1; PICP; MMP-1; TIMP-1; NT-proBNP
